Brendan McDermid | Reuters Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others. The Greg Abel-led conglomerate increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter. Delta shares tumbled 11% over that period, as rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war pressured the airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast , citing a surge in fuel costs. To be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month. Selling some Bank of America Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock. BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002 . Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter. headlines.article_text: JPMorgan Chase experiencing 'technical issue' Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points JPMorgan Chase on Monday said a "technical issue" was making some transactions take longer than usual for customers. A spokesperson for JPMorgan said the issue was not cyber-related and that it was not systemic. CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved. In this article JPM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 3:02 03:02 No indication bad actors are involved with JPMorgan Chase technical issue Closing Bell: Overtime JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical issue" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday. The bank said a "temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds. "There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC. "This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson said. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today." CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved. Still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET. A representative for U.S. Bank said that company was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays." Zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan. The outage reports come days after separate, widespread issues with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers . — CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.
